subject: POL
label: Grade 12 Humanities
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 12 Humanities Political science, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Contemporary world politics
modules.outcome: describe the cold war and globalisation
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Contemporary world politics', taught in a way that is with exam-style questions and written reasoning. The target is clear: describe the cold war and globalisation. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Place it: find where and when 'Contemporary world politics' happens, on a map, a timeline or in a local example.
Gather: read or listen to two short sources and note who is speaking and why.
Use it: describe the cold war and globalisation. Give a reason and one piece of evidence for every point.
Weigh it: say what another person might think, and why, before you decide.
modules.example: Solved: Take one source or data set. Ask five questions: who made it, when, why, what does it show, what is missing? Write three sentences using one piece of evidence each, then say what other source you would check. Method: Model run for 'Contemporary world politics'. Question: what happened, or what is the situation, and why? Sources: two short extracts, a map or table. Notes: who, what, where, when, why. Answer: three sentences, each with a reason and a piece of evidence. Check: is there a point of view that you have not considered? What a good answer looks like: facts are correct, reasons are linked to evidence, and one other point of view is named fairly.
modules.activity: About 40 to 50 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a timed paper and an error log.
modules.standard: Describe the cold war and globalisation: at least 70 percent on an exam-style task, with the method shown.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Contemporary world politics), and at which Bloom level is it?
'describe', at the Understand level. (Covered in unit 1: Contemporary world politics.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Environment, resources and human rights) run?
Weeks 28 to 36. (Covered in unit 4: Environment, resources and human rights.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A timed paper and an error log. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: talk about family, place and community.
L2: read maps and timelines; describe local government and history.
L4: analyse causes and consequences; argue from evidence.
L5: specialise in history, geography, politics or economics; write extended answers.
L6 (degree): research methods and applied social science.
L7 (postgraduate): policy, research or teaching at depth.
